subject: SLA alignment: regional uptime commitments and migration carveouts
messages:
From: Derek Wang <derek.wang@tacora.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jenn Park <jenn.park@tacora.com>, procurement@tacora.com
Date: Sun, 27 Jul 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tacora SLA request: GovCloud region uptime + monthly credit cap

Hi Monica / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the platform looks promising. Procurement asked that we put the SLA terms on the table now that we're moving forward with a pilot in the US GovCloud region. Two main asks from our side:

1) Regional uptime commitment: Tacora requires a 99.95% uptime commitment for the GovCloud region once we move out of pilot into production (we understand hosted vs dedicated differences).
2) Monthly remedy cap: our finance policy caps service credits to <= 7% of the monthly invoice for any SaaS vendor. We can't accept open-ended larger caps.

We also need a defined migration carveout — Tacora will be doing a phased data migration and may need a temporary relaxation of certain availability triggers for a 6–8 week window. Can Redwood either (a) exclude the migration window from uptime calculations, or (b) set a separate, temporary SLO for that period?

I attached our redlines to your standard SLA template (Tacora_SLA_redlines_20250727.pdf). Please let me know if there's room to meet these constraints or whether we need to budget for a dedicated/SLA uplift.

Appreciate a quick read — procurement would like a papered position before week-of-Aug 3.

Best,
Derek Wang
Head of Cloud Procurement
Tacora

--- attachment: Tacora_SLA_redlines_20250727.pdf (pdf, 134KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Derek Wang <derek.wang@tacora.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tacora SLA request: GovCloud region uptime + monthly credit cap

Hi Derek — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the redlines. Welcome, overall; we'll do our best to land something that fits procurement constraints while protecting operational realities. Quick summary of our stance and options:

- Baseline: Redwood's hosted SLA is 99.9% uptime with monthly credits formula capped at 10% of monthly service fees (standard template).
- Dedicated option: for Dedicated/reserved capacity customers we can assess a 99.95% commitment but it typically requires a pricing uplift and a capacity commitment.
- Migration carveout: we can agree to a temporary carveout window for the migration period and either exclude that window from uptime calculations or apply a separate, clearly bounded SLO. We prefer an explicit date range and a maximum of 8 weeks to keep reporting clean.

Proposed compromise (initial):
- Hosted GovCloud production: 99.9% uptime standard.
- If Tacora requires 99.95% in GovCloud, Redwood can support it on Dedicated with a negotiated monthly uplift (we can provide a % uplift estimate after confirming expected qps/throughput).
- Monthly remedy cap: we can make a one-time concession to reduce the cap to 8% for the first 3 months of production while Tacora finalizes internal risk sign-off; revert to 10% thereafter.
- Migration carveout: Redwood will exclude a defined 8-week migration window from monthly uptime calculations provided Tacora shares the migration schedule and coordinates a maintenance window of up to 12 hours/week for any disruptive activities.

Two items we need from you to move faster:
1) Target go-live date for GovCloud and the preferred 8-week migration window.
2) Whether Tacora is open to Dedicated for the higher uptime target.

I'm looping Ben (pricing) and Laura (legal) to expedite the redlines. I also attached our SLA template for reference: Redwood_SLA_Template_v1.pdf (link).

If that sounds workable I can draft a short amendment and route it for signature this week.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference

--- attachment reference: Redwood_SLA_Template_v1.pdf

From: Derek Wang <derek.wang@tacora.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jenn Park <jenn.park@tacora.com>, procurement@tacora.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 10:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tacora SLA request: GovCloud region uptime + monthly credit cap

Monica — thanks, that helps. A few follow-ups from procurement & SRE:

- Monthly remedy cap: Tacora can accept 8% for the first three months if you can commit to 8% in writing (rather than 10%).
- Migration carveout: we will share our migration timeline, but procurement wants the carveout explicitly excluded from uptime calculations and reported separately.
- Maintenance notification: we require a minimum of 72 hours for planned maintenance notifications for GovCloud services (email + Ops Slack).
- Latency target: Tacora SRE wants API P95 <= 200ms for typical inference calls in the production GovCloud region. We understand this may change depending on model size — please indicate any model families that cannot meet that threshold.

I've attached a very short procurement note that summarizes our required language. If Redwood is comfortable with the 8% cap for the first 3 months, the carveout excluded, and the 72-hour maintenance notice, procurement will move to approve.

Thanks — Derek

--- attachment: Tacora_procurement_summary_20250729.pdf (pdf, 22KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 15:36:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Tacora SLA counter — legal + pricing options

Team — internal notes summarizing quick opt-ins/risks for the record (do not forward external until we have a short amendment):

1) 8% cap for first 3 months: acceptable as a one-time concession. We should timebox it and include language that the parties will review operational metrics at month 3 to determine whether to continue reduced cap. Add clause: "temporary remedial cap" with clear end date.
2) 72-hour maintenance notice: fine. Add Ops Slack as the primary notification channel for GovCloud. Include contact points.
3) Latency P95 <= 200ms: this is model-dependent. Recommend we propose the following to Tacora: a) baseline models (up to 7B) — P95 target 200ms; b) larger models (>=13B) — best-effort and measured separately; c) any higher-latency model families will be listed in an Appendix with expected latencies. This avoids a blanket SLA we can't operationalize.
4) Migration carveout: redact from uptime calculation is acceptable provided Tacora supplies the migration schedule and agrees to a weekly sync to coordinate risk.

Pricing input (Ben): recommend we position Dedicated 99.95 at a +15–25% seat/capacity uplift depending on committed qps.

Next steps: Monica — send the 8% limited concession and the 72-hour notice language back to Derek, plus the model-latency appendix approach. If they accept, I will draft amendment language and run DocuSign.

Laura
General Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Derek Wang <derek.wang@tacora.com>, Jenn Park <jenn.park@tacora.com>, procurement@tacora.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tacora SLA request: GovCloud region uptime + monthly credit cap

Derek — quick update / agreement in principle below and next steps:

1) Monthly remedial cap: Redwood agrees to a temporary concession of 8% of monthly fees as a cap on service credits for the first three monthly billing cycles following GovCloud production go-live. This concession will automatically expire after three full billing cycles unless Tacora and Redwood mutually agree in writing to extend.

2) Migration carveout: Redwood will exclude a defined migration window (up to 8 weeks) from uptime calculations, provided Tacora delivers a schedule and coordinates weekly migration syncs with our SRE team. The migration window will be listed in the amendment.

3) Maintenance notification: Redwood will provide at least 72 hours' notice for planned disruptive maintenance affecting GovCloud; notices will be sent via email and the designated Ops Slack channel.

4) Latency P95: Redwood will commit to a measurable latency appendix. Baseline models (<=7B) — target P95 <= 200ms in GovCloud under normal load; larger model families will be documented in an Appendix as best-effort with measured baselines. We will include a small table listing model families and observed P95s.

I have attached the proposed short amendment for signature and a DocuSign link for convenience: Redwood_SLA_Amendment_Tacora_20250730.pdf and https://docusign.net/Redwood/Tacora/Envelope12345.

If this aligns with procurement's ask, please confirm and we will route the amendment. If you prefer the 99.95 commitment in writing, we can provide a Dedicated offering quote and a dedicated SLA annex.

Next steps:
- Derek/Jenn: confirm the migration window dates and whether you want to proceed on Hosted with the temporary 8% cap or request Dedicated for 99.95.
- If confirmed, we will send the amendment for signature today.

Best regards,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference
